data.reason: I follow the LLM's recommendation and keep v2 (block_k 2, hold_limit 60s). Option 1 worsens every customer measure. On-time falls from 80.8 to 80.2 (-0.6, 0/5 seeds improved), late rises from 1.8 to 2.4, p95_wait_s rises from 116 to 158, blocked s rises from 1046 to 1193, and the lowest on-time rate falls from 0.96 to 0.95. In return, road violations fall only from 26.0 to 23.6, and their safety meaning is unknown. Under K1, a change that is worse for customers needs a measured customer justification, and there is none here. Customers have no vote and would bear the whole cost. My D2/D4 condition for acting on violations was that they persist or grow. Under v2 they are 26.0, below the 28.0 accepted in D2, the 29.6 accepted in D4 and the 34.8 of period 3, so the condition is not triggered. The company vote (A ○, B ×, C ○) does not change this. Even if it passes, a company majority does not justify a measured loss to customers on the main goal, and the change fails the on-time improvement gate. C forgoes +1.3 utility, but C is not in distress. My D4 request for a targeted violation rule was for a rule that does not shift the cost onto customers, and this one does. Keeping v2 means the 26.0 violations of unknown safety meaning remain. I accept that and will keep monitoring them. D4.f2 is not settled here because its trigger (violations above 34.8) has not occurred.
assumptions: Period 5 measurements under the same seeds are representative of the trade-off in other demand levels.
Road violations at 26.0 do not indicate an acute safety hazard.
No company will materially change behaviour because this change is rejected.
unknowns: The real safety meaning of overstay road violations.
Whether another single-parameter rule could reduce violations without adding blocked time or customer waits.
Next period's demand and whether violations under v2 will rise again.
Whether the vote A ○, B ×, C ○ meets the quorum rule.
